title: Scylla Manager
description: Health check, repair and backup status of the clusters managed by Scylla Manager.

list.name: repair_task
list.label: Repair task
list.definition: query_result(scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", cron!="ad-hoc"} or (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", cron="ad-hoc"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_run_start_seconds{cluster="$cluster"} >= time() - $__range_s)))

query.query: query_result(scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", cron!="ad-hoc"} or (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", cron="ad-hoc"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_run_start_seconds{cluster="$cluster"} >= time() - $__range_s)))

list.label: Backup task

query.query: query_result(scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", cron!="ad-hoc"} or (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", cron="ad-hoc"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_run_start_seconds{cluster="$cluster"} >= time() - $__range_s)))

panels.title: SM node memory used
panels.description: Memory in use on the Scylla Manager node, measured against MemAvailable - MemFree excludes the page cache and reads alarmingly low on a healthy host.

panels.title: SM node swap used
panels.description: Swap in use on the Scylla Manager node, 0 when no swap is configured. Worth watching at lower numbers than memory or CPU: a host that has started swapping at all is already short of memory.

panels.title: SM node CPU busy
panels.description: CPU in use on the Scylla Manager node, averaged across all cores over 5 minutes - a share of the whole host, so it cannot exceed 100.

panels.title: Scylla Manager -> cluster nodes connectivity health check
CQL
panels.description: Left: nodes not healthy now. Right: nodes not healthy at some point in the selected range, so a node that dropped and recovered still counts.

panels.title: REST
panels.description: Left: nodes not healthy now. Right: nodes not healthy at some point in the selected range, so a node that dropped and recovered still counts.

panels.title: Alternator
panels.description: Left: nodes not healthy now. Right: nodes not healthy at some point in the selected range, so a node that dropped and recovered still counts. Scylla Manager reports a node as up with 0ms latency when Alternator is not enabled, so ALL UP means "not broken", not "in use".

panels.title: Nodes not healthy for the whole range
panels.description: Empty when every node was up for the whole selected range. A node that dropped and recovered is still listed, with the protocol whose check failed - or a single Agent row when the node itself could not be reached.

targets.expr: label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_cql_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -1 unless on(cluster, dc, rack, host) (min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_rest_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -2), "protocol", "CQL", "", "") or label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_rest_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -1, "protocol", "REST", "", "") or label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_alternator_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -1 unless on(cluster, dc, rack, host) (min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_rest_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -2), "protocol", "Alternator", "", "") or label_replace(min_over_time(scylla_manager_healthcheck_rest_status{cluster="$cluster", dc=~"$dc", host=~"$host"}[$__range]) == -2, "protocol", "Agent", "", "")

panels.title: CQL status
panels.description:
Up or down: this probe is dialled directly, so a failure is always the protocol's own. An unreachable node shows on the REST status instead, as a third, lower value.

Legend: Last is the state now, Min the worst in the range. Last OK with a lower Min means the node dropped and recovered - on a wide range that can be a few pixels of line.

panels.title: REST status
panels.description:
Up, Scylla's REST API down, or - lowest - the agent not answering either. This probe is proxied through the agent, so it is the one that tells an unreachable node from a broken API.

Legend: Last is the state now, Min the worst in the range. Last OK with a lower Min means the node dropped and recovered - on a wide range that can be a few pixels of line.

panels.title: Alternator status
panels.description:
Up or down: this probe is dialled directly, so a failure is always the protocol's own. An unreachable node shows on the REST status instead, as a third, lower value.

Legend: Last is the state now, Min the worst in the range. Last OK with a lower Min means the node dropped and recovered - on a wide range that can be a few pixels of line.

panels.title: Repair tasks
panels.description:
Every repair task: how its last known run went, then how it is configured. State, progress and the age of the last success describe the last run - progress is not gated on the task running, so a failed or stopped run shows how far it got.

A property left unconfigured shows the value the task will actually run with, not a blank. Scheduled tasks are always listed; ad-hoc ones only when the selected range covers their run.

targets.expr: max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}))

(max by (task) ((time() - scylla_manager_scheduler_task_last_success_seconds{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"}) and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}))) or (max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}) * 0 + 99999999)
max by (task) (scylla_manager_repair_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}))

panels.title: Repair task state
panels.description:
One row per repair task, by name - unnamed tasks fall back to their task ID. type=repair covers both vnode and tablet repair.

Hover a band to read it: a run in flight reports its percentage, a finished one its state. Nothing is written on the rows because the state is latched - on a wide range one band covers most of the row. The strip below is the colour key.

targets.expr: (max by (task) (scylla_manager_repair_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"} == 1)) or max by (task) ((scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="repair"} != 1) - 10)) * on(task) group_left(name) (topk(1, scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}) by (task))

options.content: 🔵 running · ● never executed yet · 🔴 prev execution failed · 🟡 prev execution stopped

panels.title: Time since the last successful repair
Time since the last successful repair
panels.description:
Time since each task last finished successfully: the line climbs a second per second and drops to zero when a run succeeds, so every tooth is one success and its height is the gap between two. The legend's max is the longest gap in the range.

It survives a Scylla Manager restart, so a restart does not read as a fresh success. A task that has never succeeded has no line until its first one.

targets.expr: time() - max by (name) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_last_success_seconds{cluster="$cluster"} * on(task) group_left(name) (topk(1, scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="repair", name=~"$repair_task"}) by (task)))

panels.title: Backup tasks
panels.description: Every backup task: how its last known run went, then how it is configured. Retention and Retention days are not independent - Scylla Manager keeps 3 backups only when neither is set, and otherwise honours the one that is. Scheduled tasks are always listed; ad-hoc ones only when the selected range covers their run.

targets.expr: max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}))

(max by (task) ((time() - scylla_manager_scheduler_task_last_success_seconds{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"}) and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}))) or (max by (task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}) * 0 + 99999999)
max by (task) (scylla_manager_backup_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}))

panels.title: Backup task state
panels.description:
One row per backup task, by name - unnamed tasks fall back to their task ID.

Hover a band to read it: a run in flight reports its percentage, a finished one its state. Nothing is written on the rows because the state is latched - on a wide range one band covers most of the row. The strip below is the colour key.

targets.expr: (max by (task) (scylla_manager_backup_task_progress{cluster="$cluster"} and on(task) (scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"} == 1)) or max by (task) ((scylla_manager_scheduler_task_state{cluster="$cluster", type="backup"} != 1) - 10)) * on(task) group_left(name) (topk(1, scylla_manager_scheduler_task_info{cluster="$cluster", type="backup", name=~"$backup_task"}) by (task))
